Supreme Court panel submits nationwide roadmap to modernise court infrastructure
items.summary: A Supreme Court-appointed panel on Monday placed before Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant its interim report containing a nationwide blueprint for modernising court infrastructure across the country. The CJI had constituted the Judicial Infrastructure Advisory Committee on May 12, headed by Supreme Court Justice Aravind Kumar . Its other members include Calcutta High Court Justice Debangsu Basak , Punjab and Haryana High Court Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra , Bombay High Court Justice Somasekhar Sundaresan and Central Public Works Department Director General Satinder Pal Singh. Supreme Court Secretary General Bharat Parashar serves as the Committee’s Member Secretary. According to a press statement issued by the Supreme Court, the committee has prepared a blueprint with the purpose of securing suitable government allocation for court modernisation and to address infrastructural deficiencies through substantial financial support. The Committee examined measures for establishing modern court complexes and improving the working conditions of judicial officers and administrative staff to enhance the efficiency of the justice delivery system. items.title: Madras HC co-opts former judge, lawyer as women members of State Bar Council
items.summary: The Madras High Court on Monday nominated retired Justice VM Velumani and advocate Sudarshana Sundar as two women members to be co-opted into the Bar Council of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. The nominations were made by Chief Justice of the Madras High Court, Justice SA Dharmadhikari after consultation with the elected members of the State Bar Council, a communication issued by the High Court Registrar General Deepthi Arivunithi said. Justice Velumani had served as a judge of the Madras High Court before being transferred to the Calcutta High Court, from where she retired in April 2024. The move follows the Supreme Court’s August 4 order in Yogamaya MG v Union of India , along with connected proceedings, concerning the representation of women advocates in State Bar Councils. The Court had empowered Chief Justices of the respective High Courts to nominate two women members to the State Bar Councils. The apex court’s directions came against the backdrop of concerns over inadequate representation of women in the elected bodies governing the legal profession.
